label: suspect

unstated.what: Duplicate package names must be removed inside solve_final_state's orphan add-back, not merely rejected at PrefixData.insert. The hidden test mocks _run_sat, sets add_back_map to a one-element list [MatchSpec('mkl')] (the real field is a name-to-(record, spec) dict), appends synthetic mkl and zlib records onto the pre-SAT solution_precs, and requires the returned final state to keep both names exactly once. A message-only insert fix, or a dedup that drops every orphan when add_back_map is truthy, fails; keeping zlib while dropping only the name that the SAT solution already has is new filtering on that internal path.
unstated.quote: state_returned_from_sat.add_back_map = [MatchSpec("mkl")]; ... assert "mkl" in names and "zlib" in names

instruction_covers: Final environment package records must not contain two records with the same package name
A duplicate PrefixData.insert must raise AssertionError whose message identifies the conflicting package name
Existing solver and prefix write-out semantics otherwise stay the same
notes: Insert message checks only require a non-empty AssertionError containing that record's name and not an unrelated name; the instruction states that. The solve test is the gap: conda/core/solve.py:273 adds orphans whenever add_back_map is truthy, and the test's list-shaped add_back_map plus synthetic mkl/zlib is a harness for that branch. A careful engineer grepping solve_final_state/add_back_map can find it and filter by name; the which-record-to-keep rule is not written down. Base tests/core/test_solve.py is also re-run and must still pass.
